compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Discovered from livid-painful-mosquito, which fixes the shared `run_git` wrapper (`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`) and the `ssh -V` probe (`src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py`). An AST census of `src/rebar` at origin/main `1654f3e3e53` finds 92 `subprocess.run`/`Popen`/`check_output` calls that pass `text=True` (or `universal_newlines`) and no `encoding`, in 58 files. Excluding the 3 sites fixed under livid-painful-mosquito leaves 89-90 sites in 56 files. Examples: `src/rebar/_store/project_ensures.py:42` (`_git`), `src/rebar/_store/footprint.py:158,295`, `src/rebar/_commands/verify_commit.py:141,146` (`git show -s --format=%B`, a commit body that can be non-ASCII), `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:335,528,549,566`, `src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`, `src/rebar/mirror_guard.py:230`, `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` (5 sites).

Each of them decodes child output with the locale codec: cp1252 on Windows. Non-ASCII git output (commit bodies, paths, ticket titles) is then garbled, or raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on bytes that cp1252 leaves undefined. Each site also emits `EncodingWarning` under `-X warn_default_encoding`. obtuse-phenocryst-verdin owns the sites behind current Windows-sweep failures; this bug owns the rest.

## Current census (origin/main `717c50f8b33`, 2026-11-19 PST)
An AST scan of `src/rebar` finds 85 calls in 54 files that run a child in text mode (`text=`/`universal_newlines=` not literally false) with no `encoding=`: 82 direct `subprocess.run`/`subprocess.Popen` calls (including `_authorship.subprocess.run`), the injected `run(...)` default in `src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py:55`, and 2 `dict(...)` keyword bundles later splatted into `subprocess.Popen` (`src/rebar/grounding/harness.py:165`, `src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:504`). The in-tree wrappers `run_git` and `_run_in_group` (`src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:169-232`) already decode with `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`, so calls through them are not sites. The scan rule: flag a call when it has a truthy `text`/`universal_newlines` keyword and no `encoding` keyword, and either its callee is `subprocess.<run|Popen|check_output|check_call|call>` (on a `subprocess` name or a `.subprocess` attribute) or the text keyword is the literal `True`.

## Approach
Add `encoding="utf-8"` to each of the 85 calls, keeping any `errors=` the call already passes. Every child these sites start (git, gh, ssh-keygen, ruff, uv, docker, acli, jscpd, the rebar CLI itself) writes UTF-8 or ASCII. On Linux and macOS the locale codec is already UTF-8 with strict errors, so naming UTF-8 leaves POSIX behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged and makes Windows decode the same way; strict decoding (rather than `errors="replace"`) keeps that equivalence and surfaces corrupt output instead of masking it. Routing git reads through `run_git` is not done here: it would change error handling and call shape at each site for no decoding difference, since `run_git` decodes UTF-8 too.

Enforce it with a Linux-gate test: replace `test_rebar_cli_output_is_decoded_as_utf8` in `tests/unit/test_windows_text_encoding.py`, which scans only 5 CLI-consumer files (`_CLI_CONSUMERS`, `:116-145`), with a tree-wide test applying the scan rule above to every module under `src/rebar` and asserting the list of sites is empty. The 5 files stay covered because they are under `src/rebar`.

Two files are near the 800-line module cap (`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py` 794 lines, 3 sites; `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` 780 lines, 1 site). One added keyword line per call keeps both at or under 800, which `make verify`'s module-size gate checks.

## Scope
The 54 `src/rebar` modules listed under File impact (one keyword per site), and `tests/unit/test_windows_text_encoding.py` (the tree-wide guard). `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup.py` also changes: its fake runner asserts the exact keywords of the `_jscpd.py:55` call (`:41`), so it gains `"encoding": "utf-8"`. A grep of `tests/` for exact text-mode keyword assertions (`"text": True` in a dict, `kwargs.get("text")`) finds no other test pinning an edited `src/rebar` call; `tests/scripts/test_generate_dc_wiki_legacy_outputs.py:66` pins a `scripts/` call this change does not touch. No new config key, environment variable or flag.

## Testing
- New guard: fails on the current tree (85 sites) and passes after the edit. It also flags a synthetic `subprocess.run([...], text=True)` snippet and accepts one with `encoding="utf-8"` (parametrized cases on an in-memory source string), so the rule cannot pass vacuously.
- `make verify` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The AST census above reports 0 text-mode subprocess calls without `encoding` in `src/rebar`, and a Linux-gate test enforces it.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
